audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 22, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness, prophetic, and military-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for war alliance, prophetic consensus pressure, Micaiah's sarcasm, lying-spirit vision, assault and imprisonment of dissent, battlefield disguise, targeted killing, random arrow, prolonged dying, blood and dogs, ivory palace, Jehoshaphat's reforms, qadesh translation, maritime extraction, and Ahaziah's succession.

verses.restored: They lived three years without war between Aram and Israel.
In third year Jehoshaphat king of Judah went down to king of Israel.
King of Israel said to his servants, Do you know Ramoth-gilead is ours, yet we remain still from taking it from hand of king of Aram?
He said to Jehoshaphat, Will you go with me to battle at Ramoth-gilead? Jehoshaphat said to king of Israel, I am as you, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.
Jehoshaphat said to king of Israel, Please inquire this day for word of YHWH.
King of Israel gathered prophets, about four hundred men, and said, Shall I go against Ramoth-gilead to battle, or refrain? They said, Go up, and Lord will give it into hand of king.
Jehoshaphat said, Is there not still a prophet of YHWH here, that we may inquire from him?

King of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, There is still one man through whom to inquire of YHWH, Micaiah son of Imlah, but I hate him, because he does not prophesy good concerning me, only evil. Jehoshaphat said, Let king not say so.
King of Israel called an official and said, Hurry Micaiah son of Imlah.
King of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah sat each upon his throne, clothed in robes, at threshing floor/open place at entrance of gate of Samaria, and all prophets prophesied before them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made for himself horns of iron and said, Thus says YHWH: With these you shall gore Aram until you finish it.
All prophets prophesied thus, saying, Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed, for YHWH will give it into hand of king.
Messenger who went to call Micaiah spoke to him: Look, words of prophets are good to king with one mouth. Please let your word be like word of one of them, and speak good.
Micaiah said, As YHWH lives, what YHWH says to me, that I shall speak.
He came to king, and king said to him, Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or refrain? He said, Go up and succeed; YHWH will give it into hand of king.
The king said to him, How many times must I make you swear that you speak to me only truth in name of YHWH?
He said, I saw all Israel scattered upon mountains like sheep with no shepherd. YHWH said, These have no master; let each return to his house in peace.
King of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Did I not say he would not prophesy good concerning me, only evil?
Micaiah said, Therefore hear word of YHWH: I saw YHWH sitting upon throne, and all army of heavens standing by YHWH, on right and left.
YHWH said, Who will entice Ahab so he goes up and falls at Ramoth-gilead? One said this, and another said that.
A spirit came out, stood before YHWH, and said, I will entice him.
YHWH said, By what? He said, I will go out and become a lying spirit in mouth of all his prophets. YHWH said, You shall entice and also prevail; go out and do so.
Now look, YHWH placed a lying spirit in mouth of all these prophets of yours, and YHWH spoke evil concerning you.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came near, struck Micaiah upon cheek, and said, Which way did spirit of YHWH pass from me to speak to you?
Micaiah said, Look, you shall see on day you enter inner chamber to hide.
King of Israel said, Take Micaiah and return him to Amon governor of city and Joash son of king.
Say, Thus says king: Put this one in prison and feed him bread of oppression and water of oppression until I come in peace.
Micaiah said, If returning you return in peace, YHWH did not speak by me. He said, Hear, all peoples.
King of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
King of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, I will disguise myself and enter battle, but you put on your robes. King of Israel disguised himself and entered battle.
King of Aram commanded thirty-two chariot commanders, saying, Fight neither small nor great, only king of Israel.
When chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, Surely he is king of Israel, and turned to fight him. Jehoshaphat cried out.
When chariot commanders saw he was not king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.
A man drew bow in innocence/at random and struck king of Israel between joints of armor. He said to chariot driver, Turn your hand and take me out from camp, for I am wounded.
Battle increased that day. King was held standing in chariot before Arameans and died at evening; blood of wound poured into bottom of chariot.
A cry passed through camp at setting of sun: Each to his city, and each to his land.
The king died, came to Samaria, and they buried king in Samaria.
They washed chariot by pool of Samaria, and dogs licked his blood while sex workers/bathers washed there, according to word YHWH spoke.
Rest of acts of Ahab, all he did, ivory house he built, and all cities he built—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Israel?
Ahab lay with his ancestors, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.
Jehoshaphat son of Asa began to reign over Judah in fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he began to reign and reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
He walked in all way of Asa his father, did not turn aside, doing upright in eyes of YHWH. Yet high places were not removed; people still sacrificed and burned incense at high places.
Jehoshaphat made peace with king of Israel.
Rest of acts of Jehoshaphat, might he showed, and how he fought—are they not written in book of chronicles of kings of Judah?
The remainder of male cult personnel/consecrated persons who remained in days of Asa his father he removed from land.
There was no king in Edom; a deputy was king.
Jehoshaphat made Tarshish ships to go to Ophir for gold, but they did not go, for ships were broken at Ezion-geber.
Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, Let my servants go with your servants in ships. Jehoshaphat was not willing.
Jehoshaphat lay with his ancestors and was buried with ancestors in City of David his ancestor. Jehoram his son reigned in his place.
Ahaziah son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah and reigned two years over Israel.
He did evil in eyes of YHWH and walked in way of his father, way of his mother, and way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.
He served Baal, bowed to him, and provoked YHWH, Divine of Israel, according to all his father did.

translation_notes: Four hundred prophets speak with one voice in a royal public setting, while the messenger pressures Micaiah to conform. Consensus under patronage and threat is not reliable discernment by itself.
Micaiah's first answer appears sarcastic, and Ahab recognizes it. Prophetic speech may include irony, but vulnerable audiences need clarity rather than manipulative ambiguity.

The heavenly council and lying-spirit vision presents the Divine authorizing deception. This is a major theological difficulty and must not justify lying, entrapment, false prophecy, or claiming that misinformation is sacred strategy.
Zedekiah strikes Micaiah, and Ahab imprisons him on reduced food and water. Assault and detention of a dissenting prophet expose how regimes manage unwelcome truth.
Ahab disguises himself while asking Jehoshaphat to remain visibly royal, shifting battlefield risk onto his ally. Religious alliance does not excuse deception.
The unnamed archer shoots without knowing the target. Ahab's death is not the archer's moral triumph, and ordinary soldiers are not mere instruments of prophecy.
Ahab is kept upright in the chariot while bleeding until evening. The scene is prolonged bodily suffering, not a satisfying spectacle.
Dogs licking blood and the washing scene should not become sexualized contempt toward sex workers or bathers; the Hebrew detail is textually uncertain.
Verse 46 again uses qadesh and must not be weaponized against LGBTQ people.
Jehoshaphat's failed Ophir fleet reflects royal gold ambition, maritime labor risk, and ecological extraction. Broken ships are not proof that every failed venture is Divine judgment.
Ahaziah's conduct is linked to both parents, but Jezebel must not become the gendered container for dynastic responsibility.
safety_note: Protect dissenters from pressure, assault, imprisonment, and starvation. Do not use the lying-spirit vision to justify deception, prophetic manipulation, or certainty that opposing voices are divinely deluded. Do not weaponize qadesh against LGBTQ people or turn Ahab's death into revenge entertainment.
